name: Medicine and Surgery
summary: Train to become a doctor: the sciences of the human body, how disease works, and years of supervised clinical practice.
overview:
Medicine and Surgery (MBBS or MBChB) trains you to diagnose and treat illness. It is long and demanding, with heavy memorisation early on and long clinical hours later, but it leads to one of the most secure and respected professions anywhere.

The early years cover the basic medical sciences: anatomy, physiology and biochemistry. The middle years cover how disease works and how drugs act (pathology, pharmacology, microbiology, haematology). The final years are spent on clinical rotations in hospitals and communities, learning medicine, surgery, obstetrics and gynaecology, paediatrics, psychiatry and public health on real patients.

After graduating you still need supervised practice before full registration: housemanship in Nigeria, the Foundation Programme in the UK, or residency in the US.
durationNotes: 6 years in Nigeria (MBBS), then a 1-year housemanship. Usually 5 years in the UK (6 with an intercalated degree). In the US, medicine is a 4-year graduate degree (MD) taken after a bachelor's.

entryRequirements.notes: Credits in all five. Most universities require them in one sitting, and competition means high UTME and post-UTME scores.

subjects: One more academic subject (Maths or Physics are common)
entryRequirements.notes: Usually A*AA to AAA, plus the UCAT admissions test and an interview. Some schools accept Chemistry with one other science.
In the US you first complete a bachelor's degree with pre-med courses, then take the MCAT to apply to medical school.

careers.title: Hospital doctor
careers.description: Specialises through residency in areas like internal medicine, surgery, paediatrics or emergency medicine.

careers.title: General practitioner (family doctor)
careers.description: Provides first-contact care in the community and manages long-term conditions.

careers.title: Surgeon
careers.description: Operates to treat injury and disease after years of specialist surgical training.

careers.title: Public health physician
careers.description: Works on disease prevention, outbreaks and health policy for whole populations.

careers.title: Medical researcher
careers.description: Runs clinical trials or laboratory research to develop new treatments.

careers.title: Pharmaceutical or health-tech advisor
careers.description: Brings clinical expertise to drug development, health insurance or digital health companies.

stages.title: Year 1
stages.summary: Pre-medical sciences: the biology, chemistry and physics that medicine builds on.

stages.title: Year 2
stages.summary: Basic medical sciences: the structure and function of the healthy body.

stages.title: Year 3
stages.summary: Finish the pre-clinical sciences and sit Part I MBBS.

stages.title: Year 4
stages.summary: How disease works and how drugs act, plus your first clinical skills. Ends with Part II MBBS.

stages.title: Year 5
stages.summary: Clinical rotations in medicine, surgery, psychiatry and community health.

stages.title: Final year
stages.summary: Obstetrics, paediatrics, an elective posting and Final MBBS.

nodes.title: General Biology
nodes.description: Cell biology, genetics, evolution and basic physiology. This is the base for anatomy, physiology and biochemistry next year.

nodes.title: General and Organic Chemistry
nodes.description: Atomic structure, bonding, acids and bases, reaction rates and organic chemistry. You'll need it for biochemistry and pharmacology.

nodes.title: General Physics
nodes.description: Mechanics, fluids, electricity, optics and radiation. It explains blood flow, nerve signals, how the eye works and how imaging machines see inside the body.

nodes.title: Medical terminology
nodes.description: Learn the Greek and Latin roots, prefixes and suffixes medical words are built from. Lectures in later years get much easier once these are automatic.

nodes.title: Gross Anatomy
nodes.description: The structure of the human body region by region, usually learned through cadaver dissection: upper and lower limbs, thorax, abdomen, pelvis, head and neck.

nodes.title: Histology and Embryology
nodes.description: Histology is the microscopic structure of tissues; embryology is how the body develops before birth. Together they explain the normal structure that pathology later compares against.

nodes.title: Physiology
nodes.description: How the healthy body works, system by system: cells, nerves and muscle, blood, heart and circulation, lungs, kidneys, gut and hormones.

nodes.title: Medical Biochemistry
nodes.description: The chemistry of life: proteins and enzymes, how cells make and use energy, metabolism of carbohydrates, fats and amino acids, and molecular biology.

nodes.title: First aid and Basic Life Support
nodes.description: Learn CPR and basic first aid early. It's a skill you can use immediately, and many schools expect it before clinical placements.

nodes.title: Neuroanatomy and Neuroscience
nodes.description: The brain, spinal cord and nerves: their structure, pathways and how damage in a specific place produces specific symptoms.

nodes.title: Medical Ethics and Professionalism
nodes.description: The principles that guide doctors' decisions: consent, confidentiality, capacity, and professional duties set out by regulators like the MDCN and GMC.

resources.title: WMA Declaration of Geneva (World Medical Association)

nodes.title: Research Methods and Biostatistics
nodes.description: How to read and judge medical research: study designs, bias, basic statistics and evidence-based medicine.

nodes.title: Part I MBBS examination
nodes.description: The professional exam covering anatomy, physiology and biochemistry. You must pass it to move on to the clinical part of the course, so plan revision months ahead.

nodes.title: Pathology
nodes.description: How disease changes cells, tissues and organs: inflammation, repair, tumours and the disease processes of each body system.

resources.title: WebPath: Internet Pathology Laboratory (University of Utah)

nodes.title: Pharmacology and Therapeutics
nodes.description: How drugs work in the body and how the body handles drugs, plus the main drug classes for each system and how to prescribe safely.

resources.title: WHO Model List of Essential Medicines

nodes.title: Medical Microbiology and Parasitology
nodes.description: The bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites that cause disease, how they're identified in the lab, and how infections are treated and prevented, including malaria and other tropical diseases.

nodes.title: Haematology and Blood Transfusion
nodes.description: Disorders of blood cells and clotting, such as anaemias (including sickle cell disease), leukaemias and bleeding disorders, plus safe blood transfusion.

resources.title: ASH Image Bank (American Society of Hematology)

nodes.title: Chemical Pathology
nodes.description: Using blood and urine chemistry to diagnose and monitor disease: electrolytes, kidney and liver function, glucose, lipids and hormones.

nodes.title: Introduction to Clinical Medicine
nodes.description: Your first steps with patients: taking a history, examining each body system, presenting cases and basic procedures.

resources.title: OSCE and clinical skills guides (Geeky Medics)

nodes.title: Internal Medicine
nodes.description: Diagnosing and managing adult disease across cardiology, respiratory, gastroenterology, nephrology, neurology, endocrinology and infectious disease.

nodes.title: Surgery
nodes.description: General surgery and its specialties: the acute abdomen, trauma, perioperative care, wounds, and assisting in theatre.

nodes.title: Community Medicine and Public Health
nodes.description: Health at the population level: epidemiology, disease prevention, immunisation, nutrition, primary health care and health systems. Usually includes a rural community posting.

resources.title: Epidemiology: The Basic Science of Public Health (Coursera, free to audit)

nodes.title: Psychiatry
nodes.description: Assessing and treating mental illness: the mental state examination, mood and psychotic disorders, substance use, and risk assessment.

nodes.title: Specialty postings
nodes.description: Shorter rotations in smaller specialties: anaesthesia, radiology, ophthalmology, ENT, dermatology and emergency medicine.

nodes.title: Obstetrics and Gynaecology
nodes.description: Pregnancy, childbirth and women's reproductive health: antenatal care, normal and complicated labour, obstetric emergencies and gynaecological conditions.

nodes.title: Paediatrics
nodes.description: Medicine for newborns, children and adolescents: growth and development, neonatal care, childhood infections, malnutrition and immunisation.

nodes.title: Elective posting
nodes.description: A few weeks in a specialty or hospital of your choice, sometimes abroad. Use it to explore a career interest or a different health system.

nodes.title: Final MBBS examination
nodes.description: The final professional exam across medicine, surgery, obstetrics and gynaecology, paediatrics and community medicine, with written papers, long and short cases, OSCEs and vivas.

nodes.title: After graduation: housemanship and beyond
nodes.description: What comes next: provisional registration and a 1-year housemanship then NYSC in Nigeria, the Foundation Programme in the UK, or USMLE and residency in the US.

resources.title: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
